title: Manipal Health's Rs 9,275-Crore IPO Leads Packed Week on Dalal Street With Nine Offerings and Seven Listings
excerpt: India's primary market enters its busiest stretch of the year as Temasek-backed Manipal Health opens on July 29, Indo-MIM nears listing with strong subscription and several SME issues launch.
body:
• Manipal Health Enterprises, India's second-largest hospital chain, will open its Rs 9,275-crore IPO on July 29 at a price band of Rs 560–590 per share
  • Indo-MIM, the world's largest metal injection moulding manufacturer, saw its Rs 3,812-crore IPO oversubscribed at 2.24x by Day 2, with listing on July 30
  • At least nine public issues are lined up for the week, with seven listings scheduled across mainboard and SME segments
  • The IPO surge comes despite market headwinds from Middle East tensions and a five-session losing streak on Indian bourses

Manipal Health: The Marquee Offering

Temasek-backed Manipal Health Enterprises will open India's second-largest IPO of 2026 on Tuesday, July 29, aiming to raise up to Rs 9,275 crore at the upper end of its Rs 560–590 per share price band. The three-day issue closes on July 31, with anchor investor bidding on July 28.

The Bengaluru-based hospital chain, which operates 49 hospitals with over 13,000 beds across 14 states, plans to use a significant chunk of the Rs 8,000-crore fresh issue to become net debt-free. The company currently carries about Rs 10,000 crore in gross debt against Rs 2,500 crore in cash — the IPO proceeds would eliminate the gap entirely.

"We believe good companies, good stories would still attract investors. We started the exercise six, seven months ago and the war happened after that."

— Dilip Jose, MD and CEO, Manipal Health Enterprises

At the upper end, the IPO values Manipal Health at roughly Rs 77,600 crore (about $8 billion). Temasek, which holds a 51% stake, will remain the largest shareholder after the offering, while the founding Pai family retains around 30%. The company reported revenue of Rs 10,336 crore in FY26 — a 67% jump from FY24 — with a net profit of Rs 917 crore. Its network treated 7.63 million patients last fiscal year with a team of 11,064 doctors.

Manipal also plans to spend Rs 4,000 crore to add 2,400 beds to its network over the next three to four years, targeting expansion in Kerala, Hyderabad and the NCR region.

Indo-MIM Draws Strong Demand

While Manipal Health prepares for its debut, Indo-MIM's Rs 3,812-crore IPO has already attracted robust interest. By Day 2, the issue was oversubscribed at 2.24 times overall, with the non-institutional investor (NII) category surging past 8 times. The company, which holds a 6.8% share of the global metal injection moulding market, posted FY26 revenue of Rs 4,193 crore — up nearly 26% year-on-year — with an adjusted profit after tax of Rs 612 crore.

Shares of Indo-MIM, along with Xtranet Technologies (Rs 170-crore issue) and Lohia Corp (Rs 1,102-crore OFS), are all set to list on July 30.

SME Segment Stays Active

The small and medium enterprise segment continues to see steady deal flow. Issues opening this week include Propshop Events and Exhibitions (Rs 29 crore) and Advance Technoforge (Rs 24 crore) on July 27, with H.R. Hygiene Products (Rs 54 crore) and Poojaa Precision Engineering (Rs 160 crore) following close behind. Dhaval Packaging (Rs 36 crore) and Fusion Klassroom Edutech (Rs 39 crore) open later in the week.

Cube Highways Trust, an infrastructure investment trust backed by I Squared Capital, will also list on July 31 after its Rs 2,300-crore issue closed earlier this week.

Market Context

The IPO flurry arrives against a mixed market backdrop. Indian benchmarks extended their losing streak to five sessions last week, with the Sensex and Nifty under pressure from rising oil prices, disappointing Q1 earnings in select pockets and broader global risk aversion tied to the Middle East conflict. The Nasdaq dropped 2.1% for the week on AI spending fears, adding to cross-border caution.

Yet primary market activity tells a different story. Over a dozen IPOs are lined up for August, aiming to raise upwards of Rs 25,000 crore collectively. With 36 companies having already launched IPOs in 2026, dealmakers say the pipeline reflects sustained confidence in India's long-term equity story — even as secondary markets wobble.
